content: The primary goal in the prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) is to reduce maternal mortality. Misoprostol offers a significant public health advantage over injectable medications because it can be more easily distributed at the community level. However, misoprostol may cause adverse effects unrelated to blood loss, which could influence mortality or severe morbidity. Therefore, it is critical to maintain ongoing surveillance of all relevant evidence from randomized trials. This is especially important as misoprostol is being widely introduced for PPH prevention in low-income countries and is also commonly used for PPH treatment in well-resourced settings. The objective of this review was to assess maternal deaths and severe morbidity in all randomized trials of misoprostol for the prevention or treatment of PPH. The Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register was searched on January 11, 2013, to identify relevant studies. Randomized trials involving pregnant women who received misoprostol in the postpartum period, compared to placebo, no treatment, or other uterotonics, were included if they reported on maternal death, severe morbidity, or pyrexia. Although clusterand quasi-randomized trials were planned for inclusion to achieve robust estimates of maternal mortality, none were identified for this version of the review. Future updates may include trials reported only as abstracts if sufficient information is available. Two independent reviewers assessed the trials for inclusion and extracted data. A total of 78 studies involving 59,216 women were included, while 34 studies were excluded. There was no statistically significant difference in maternal mortality between misoprostol and control groups overall. Specifically, in 31 studies, there were 11 deaths among 19,715 women in the misoprostol group compared to 4 deaths among 20,076 women in the control group (risk ratio [RR] 2.08, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.82 to 5.28). Similarly, no significant difference in maternal mortality was observed in trials comparing misoprostol to placebo (10 studies; RR 2.70, 95% CI 0.72 to 10.11) or to other uterotonics (21 studies; RR 1.54, 95% CI 0.40 to 5.92). Notably, all 11 deaths in the misoprostol groups occurred in studies using doses of 600 µg or higher. There was a statistically significant increase in the composite outcome of maternal death or severe morbidity when misoprostol was compared to placebo (12 studies; average RR 1.70, 95% CI 1.02 to 2.81). However, no significant difference was observed when misoprostol was compared to other uterotonics (17 studies; average RR 1.50, 95% CI 0.50 to 4.52). When hyperpyrexia was excluded from the composite outcome in exploratory analyses, no significant differences were found in either comparison. Pyrexia (fever > 38°C) was significantly more common with misoprostol compared to controls. Across 56 studies, 10.8% of women in the misoprostol group experienced pyrexia (2,776/25,647) compared to 2.3% in the control group (614/26,800), with an average RR of 3.97 (95% CI 3.13 to 5.04). The risk of pyrexia was higher in trials using misoprostol doses of 600 µg or more (27 studies; RR 4.64, 95% CI 3.33 to 6.46) compared to those using doses of 400 µg or less (31 studies; RR 3.07, 95% CI 2.25 to 4.18). In conclusion, misoprostol does not appear to significantly increase or reduce severe morbidity (excluding hyperpyrexia) or maternal mortality when used for the prevention or treatment of PPH. However, it is associated with an increased risk of pyrexia, particularly at doses of 600 µg or higher. Given that misoprostol is often used prophylactically in large numbers of healthy women, minimizing adverse effects is of paramount importance. These findings support the use of the lowest effective dose of misoprostol. As with any new medication being used on a large scale, ongoing vigilance for adverse effects is essential. Large randomized trials are needed to further clarify the relative effectiveness and risks associated with different dosages of misoprostol.
